title: Strict fd-dup target parsing for >& and <&
description: DupRedirect currently classifies targets with Integer(target, 10), accepting signed strings like +1 and treating -1 as numeric. dash reports Bad fd number and exits 2 for echo x >&+1 and echo x >&-1. Relevant code: lib/rush/redirection/dup_redirect.rb numeric/source.
acceptance_criteria: Dup redirect target classifier accepts only '-' or unsigned decimal fd words; signed/non-fd words produce the correct redirect/BuiltinError behavior; differential cases for >&+1, >&-1, <&+0, <&-1 (regular command and special/no-command variants where relevant) match dash or documented POSIX divergence; bundle exec rake is green.
close_reason: Dup redirect targets now accept only unsigned decimal fd words (or '-' handled by close form). Signed targets like >&+1, >&-1, <&+0, <&-1 raise Bad fd number and match dash; unit and differential coverage added; full rake green.

title: Lexer state stack for nested case/for/compound contexts
description: LexState documents that modes are single-token/not a stack, so nested constructs inside case bodies can be misclassified. Reproducer: case x in x) for i in a b; do echo $i; done;; esac parses/runs in dash but rush reports syntax error near WORD i. Relevant code: lib/rush/lexer/lex_state.rb, lib/rush/lexer/token_classifier.rb, grammar/shell.y.
acceptance_criteria: Lexer/parser context tracking handles nested for/case/if/while/function constructs inside case bodies and other compound bodies; focused differential corpus includes nested case/for examples; no regressions in alias/reserved-word classification; bundle exec rake is green.
close_reason: LexState now tracks nested compound open/close contexts and returns to the surrounding case body after nested for/case/if constructs, so nested headers classify NAME/In/Esac correctly. Added lexer specs and dash differential cases for nested for/case/if in case arms; full rake green.

title: Closed stderr must not mask command-not-found/exec failure status
description: Focused architectural review found that diagnostics written after ENOENT/EACCES can raise Errno::EBADF when fd 2 is closed, masking the required POSIX status. Evidence: no-such-rush-xyz 2>&- returns a Ruby stacktrace/status 1 instead of dash's 127; exec no-such-rush-xyz 2>&- returns 1 instead of 127. Relevant code: lib/rush/external.rb error_status, lib/rush/builtins/exec.rb abort_exec, lib/rush/command_runner.rb builtin EBADF handling, lib/rush/fd_entry.rb closed stream.
acceptance_criteria: Diagnostics for external lookup failure and failed exec are best-effort when stderr is closed; no Ruby stacktrace leaks; focused differential cases for no-such 2>&- and exec no-such 2>&- match dash on [stdout, exitstatus]; bundle exec rake is green.
close_reason: External lookup and exec failure diagnostics are now best-effort when fd 2 is closed: EBADF while reporting is swallowed, preserving 127/126 status and preventing stack traces. Added unit and dash differential cases for closed stderr; full rake green.

title: exec redirect-only permanence (exec >file / 3>file / 2>&1 persist)
description:
Last path-2 piece (M5). exec with only redirects (no command word) must apply them permanently to the shell IO table for the rest of the session.

Root cause already diagnosed: Executor#with_redirects ensure closes the file opened over base (io.ios - base.ios), undoing exec's replace_io. The dup case (exec 2>&1) already works because no new stream is opened.

Fix: skip the close when the executor committed the io (io.equal?(@io) after replace_io). Verify bit-exact vs dash: exec >f / 3>f / 2>&1 / 9<f persist; subshell isolation (( exec >f ); after) does not leak; bad-path exec already fatal (7aj). One slice, green rake.
close_reason: exec redirect-only permanence: with_redirects skips closing the io exec committed via replace_io (io.equal?(@io)); verified vs dash + corpus + unit test; green rake, 100% cov

title: function-call redirects not applied to the function body
description: `f(){ echo body; }; f >file` — dash sends body to file; rush prints body to stdout. CommandRunner#run_function does not thread the redirected io into the function body (dispatch passes io to builtin/External but run_function ignores it). Likely fix: run the function body under executor.with_io(io). Found by the 7aj redirect fuzz; orthogonal to 7aj. Verify bit-exact vs dash + add to differential corpus.
close_reason: run_function now binds the call's redirect io to the body via with_io, but only when a redirect layered a new table (io != base) so exec inside a no-redirect call still persists; verified vs dash incl. exec-scope cases + corpus + unit; green rake 100% cov

title: Phase 2 — Intermediate
close_reason: Phase 2 (Intermediate) complete: all sub-issues (.1 exec-redirect permanence, .2 function-call redirects, .3 shift abort, .4 hash/times/set -v) landed across slices 7ak-7an, each verified vs dash with green rake

title: Assignment command substitutions should observe same-command redirections
description: Dash applies same-command redirections to assignment command substitutions attached to a command or to a no-command assignment/redirect simple command: X=$(echo err >&2) true 2>f and X=$(echo err >&2) 2>f write err to f. rush currently emits err on the shell stderr for the no-command case because RedirectScope yields an IoTable without rebinding Executor#io while CommandAssignments expands RHS values. Use AST::SimpleCommand#parts/source-order context as needed, but preserve POSIX command-word expansion behaviour where echo $(echo err >&2) 2>f leaves f empty.
acceptance_criteria: Add differential coverage for assignment command substitutions with same-command redirections (command and no-command forms); fix CommandRunner/RedirectScope so assignment RHS expansion observes the redirected IoTable without making command-word expansion observe it; full bundle exec rake green.
close_reason: Fixed assignment RHS expansion under same-command redirections: CommandRunner now rebinds Executor#io to the redirected IoTable only while persisting bare assignments or building the external command environment, leaving argv expansion before redirection. Added dash differential coverage for command-word substitution, external assignment, and no-command assignment/redirect forms; full rake green.

title: Slice: finish getopts diagnostics and silent mode
description: Complete getopts POSIX error handling: invalid options, missing required arguments, leading-colon silent mode, OPTARG set/unset details, diagnostics, and OPTIND reset behaviour.
design: Layer exact dash/POSIX error cases onto the core getopts parser. Normal mode emits diagnostics and stores ? in the name variable; silent mode suppresses diagnostics and uses OPTARG plus ?/: results. Honour manual OPTIND=1 reset by resetting the internal cluster cursor.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid-option and missing-argument cases match dash in normal and silent modes; OPTARG is set/unset exactly; diagnostics go to stderr only when expected; OPTIND=1 reset permits reparsing; unit specs and dash differential coverage pass; bundle exec rake green.
close_reason: Implemented getopts diagnostics and silent mode in the same slice: invalid options and missing arguments match dash/POSIX, with OPTARG set/unset and diagnostics suppressed in leading-colon mode. Unit and dash differential coverage added; full rake green.

title: Slice: implement getopts core parser state
description: Add the getopts regular builtin with persistent OPTIND-driven parsing over positional parameters or explicit args, including clustered short options and options that take arguments.
design: Register Builtins::Getopts. Initialize OPTIND=1 in shell state. Add a small GetoptsState (or equivalent ShellState component) for the intra-argument cursor needed by clusters like -ab. Support getopts optstring name [args...] without silent/error-mode polish beyond the core success/end-of-options path.
acceptance_criteria: getopts parses simple and clustered options; options with attached or following arguments set OPTARG; OPTIND advances like dash; explicit args override positional parameters; end-of-options returns non-zero and sets the name variable like dash; unit specs and dash differential coverage pass; bundle exec rake green.
close_reason: Implemented getopts builtin core parser state: OPTIND initialization, hidden cluster cursor, positional vs explicit args, clustered options, required args attached/following, end-of-options, and OPTIND reset. Unit and dash differential coverage added; full rake green.

title: Slice: implement noclobber redirection semantics
description: Implement set -C / set -o noclobber for ordinary > redirections while preserving >| as the explicit clobber override. Keep the change local to shell options and file redirection opening.
design: Add C/noclobber to Builtins::Set and Options. Teach FileRedirect to use an exclusive-create open path for :out under noclobber; append/input/readwrite/dup/heredoc are unaffected, and :clobber (>|) bypasses noclobber. Prefer atomic File::EXCL over stat-then-open.
acceptance_criteria: set -C prevents > from truncating an existing regular file and leaves it unchanged; >| still truncates; set +C restores ordinary > behaviour; missing/permission errors remain redirection errors; unit specs and dash differential coverage pass; bundle exec rake green.
close_reason: Implemented noclobber redirection semantics: set -C/-o noclobber toggles :noclobber, ordinary > uses exclusive-create mode under noclobber, >| bypasses, and +C restores truncation. Unit and dash differential coverage added; full rake green.

title: RedirectScope must close overwritten owned redirection streams
description: Executor#with_redirects folds redirects into a final IoTable and cleanup closes only entries present in that final table but absent from base. If a redirect opens an owned stream and a later redirect overwrites the fd (e.g. : >f 1>&2 or exec >f 1>&2), the opened entry can be lost until GC/process exit. Relevant code: lib/rush/executor.rb with_redirects/close_redirect_io, lib/rush/io_table.rb close_opened_over, redirection file/heredoc appliers.
acceptance_criteria: Redirect application tracks all owned streams opened in the current redirection scope and closes/releases superseded ones exactly once; exec redirect permanence still works for final committed streams; unit tests cover overwritten per-command and exec redirects; differential tests added where behavior is observable; bundle exec rake is green.
close_reason: Tracked owned entries opened by each redirection step, closed superseded streams even when overwritten before final table, and preserved redirect-only exec permanence for final committed streams. Added IoTable and Executor regression specs; full rake green.

title: Implement non-interactive async '&' execution semantics and $!
description: AST::ListEntry records async, but AST::List#run_entry still executes the command synchronously in a tested context. Reproducer: false & echo rc=$? prints rc=1 in rush, rc=0 in dash. $! is currently nil in ShellParameters. Implement POSIX non-interactive background execution separately from full Phase 4 job control.
acceptance_criteria: Commands terminated by & start asynchronously, the shell reports launch status semantics compatible with dash, $! resolves to the last background pid, and non-interactive behavior is covered without requiring full job control; focused differential cases pass; bundle exec rake is green.
close_reason: Implemented non-interactive async list launch via forked background subshells, parent launch-success status, and $! tracking for the latest background pid. Added unit coverage plus dash differential cases for false & status and non-empty $!; full rake green.

title: Implement POSIX -c argv semantics for $0 and positional parameters
description: rush -c currently leaves ShellState name as 'rush' and positionals empty. dash/POSIX use argv after -c: first operand becomes $0 and remaining operands become $1..$n. Reproducer: rush -c 'echo "$0:$1:$#"' name a b prints rush::0, dash prints name:a:2. Relevant code: lib/rush/source.rb, lib/rush/shell_state.rb, lib/rush/shell_parameters.rb.
acceptance_criteria: -c command_name arg... initializes $0 and positionals like dash/POSIX; stdin source behavior remains unchanged; differential tests cover $0/$1/$# under -c; bundle exec rake is green.
close_reason: Implemented POSIX -c operand mapping: command_name initializes $0 and remaining operands initialize positional parameters, while stdin source behavior remains unchanged. Added unit and dash differential coverage; full rake green.

title: Sorbet: inline sig {} types + srb tc in rake gate (independent from RBS/Steep)
description: Second, INDEPENDENT type system alongside RBS/Steep (rush-211.2). Per user directive: two formats for two tools, signatures deliberately NOT shared. Sorbet uses the inline sig {} DSL (extend T::Sig; sorbet-runtime dependency accepted) with # typed: sigils; 'srb tc' green in the default rake gate. Bootstrap via srb init / tapioca; raise # typed: levels gradually (false -> true -> strict). sorbet 0.6.x maintained, free.
design: Two independent checkers over the same code by design (path A from the types discussion): RBS in sig/*.rbs for Steep, inline sig {} for Sorbet. Drift between the two sig sets is EXPECTED AND WELCOME — divergences are food for thought / signal worth examining, NOT bugs to reconcile or DRY away. Accepts what rush-211 originally rejected (runtime dep + code pollution): that trade is the explicit user choice. Reasonableness of the dual-maintenance approach to be evaluated separately by the user.
acceptance_criteria: srb tc green in default rake (separate gate from steep check); lib/ at # typed: true or higher; sig {} on the public API; documented as an independent gate; no attempt to keep Sorbet and RBS sigs in lockstep.
notes: Slice 3 (inline sig {} foundation) done: RBS bridge sig/sorbet_dsl.rbs lets Steep ignore the Sorbet DSL on shared .rb (block self = T::Private::DeclBuilder is the key; [self: untyped] does NOT bind). require 'sorbet-runtime' in lib/rush.rb. First real sig {} on Status (extend T::Sig in both .rb and .rbs). Both checkers green + runtime enforces. Two findings: (1) sorbet-runtime is a RUNTIME check RBS lacks -> instance_double clashes; prod validates, tests install call_validation_error_handler no-op. (2) typing Status rippled into loop runners (srb.help/7001 loop var type change) -> T.let pin. Bridge makes rest of sig {} rollout mechanical. REMAINING: roll sig {} across public API class-by-class; optionally reclaim the 5 typed:false files via T.unsafe now that the bridge exists.
close_reason: Done. Sorbet is a fully independent second type checker alongside RBS/Steep: srb (raw sorbet-static binary) green in the default rake gate next to steep; lib at # typed: true (116/121 files; 5 documented # typed: false for genuine Steep-vs-Sorbet drift); inline sig {} comprehensive across the public API (110 classes, ~690 sig blocks) via the sig/sorbet_dsl.rbs bridge that lets Steep ignore the Sorbet DSL on shared .rb; runtime validation on in prod, neutralized for RSpec doubles in tests. Drift between the two sig sets is catalogued in docs/journal.md, NOT reconciled (per charter). Commits a441352..d7ba225.

title: Differential harness: close inherited fds (close_others) to stop >&9 flakiness
description: The differential snippets 'true >&9', 'echo x >&9' redirect to an fd never opened in-shell. When the rspec launcher leaks an open fd 9 (e.g. an interactive shell that ran exec 9>...), dash dups the real inherited fd (rc 0) but rush, which only tracks fds it opened, errors (rc 2) — so the test flaked depending on the launcher's fd table. Spawn both subprocesses with close_others: true so the comparison is hermetic and >&9 means 'unopened fd' for both. Not caused by the test/( ) grouping work; that commit only shifted example indices.
close_reason: Closed

title: Honour parent-inherited fds in >&n / <&n redirections (dash-compat)
description: rush resolves a redirection's source fd in n>&m / n<&m only against its own IoTable (fds 0/1/2 plus those opened in-shell via exec). An fd >= 3 inherited open from the parent process is invisible, so 'true >&9' with fd 9 inherited-open raises RedirectError -> status 2, where dash dups the real OS fd and succeeds (0). POSIX and dash operate on the actual process fd table. Goal: make >&n / <&n fall back to the real inherited fd when n is not tracked by the IoTable, matching dash.
design: IoTable currently abstracts logical fds -> IO objects and is the boundary for redirects and child-spawn fd setup. To honour inherited fds, when n is absent from the table, probe the real OS fd (e.g. IO.for_fd(n) guarded by a fcntl F_GETFD / rescue Errno::EBADF) and dup from it instead of erroring; a genuinely-closed fd must still error like dash. Open design question: whether raw OS fds should leak through the IoTable abstraction, and how this interacts with subshell/child fd inheritance and close_redirect bookkeeping.
acceptance_criteria: exec 9>/dev/null; true >&9; echo $?  -> 0 (matches dash); an inherited-open fd works as a redirect source/target; a genuinely-closed fd still errors (status 2). Add specs that control fd state explicitly (the differential harness deliberately closes inherited fds per rush-7ue, so cover this with targeted unit/integration specs rather than ambient-fd differential cases).
close_reason: Implemented inherited fd probing for dup redirects: absent source fds now fall back to a non-owning IO.for_fd wrapper, while logically closed fds still fail. Added fake-system unit coverage and real subprocess specs with explicit fd 9 inheritance/closure.

title: test/[ : accept surrounding whitespace in integer operands (dash/bash-compat)
description: POSIX leaves the lexical form of test's integer operands unspecified (the test page defines no integer syntax and never mentions leading/trailing blanks). dash AND bash both accept surrounding whitespace via their C strtol heritage: [ ' 5' -eq 5 ] and [ '5 ' -eq 5 ] succeed. rush's TestExpr#to_int used /\\A[+-]?\\d+\\z/ and rejected them with exit 2. Both behaviours are conformant; matching dash+bash maximises real-script compatibility. Fix: widen the validator to /\\A\\s*[+-]?\\d+\\s*\\z/ (String#to_i already tolerates the padding); underscores (1_000) and hex (0x10) stay rejected, matching dash.
close_reason: Fixed: to_int validator widened to allow surrounding whitespace; differential-verified against dash.

title: test/[ : support recursive ( ) grouping and >4-arg expressions (dash-compat)
description: Rush::Builtins::TestExpr implements only POSIX's flat 0-4 argument algorithm and hard-caps at 4 args (evaluate raises 'too many arguments' for args.size > 4). dash extends this: it recurses through ( ... ) groupings of any length. So [ ( a = a ) ] (5 args) gives exit 0 in dash but exit 2 in rush, and nested [ ( ( ) ) ] also diverges. This is pre-existing (the old SIZES/four? code behaved identically) and POSIX leaves >4 args unspecified, so it is low priority. NOTE: after the recursive-evaluate refactor this is now nearly free to fix — drop the 'args.size > 4' cap and let the !/wrapped? peeling recurse on any length; add differential cases for [ ( a = a ) ], [ ( ( -n x ) ) ], [ ! ( a = b ) ].
close_reason: Closed

title: heredoc does not expand $((...)) arithmetic
description: In a here-document body, $((expr)) is treated as command substitution of (expr), not arithmetic expansion. e.g. cat <<E ... $((1+1)) ... E yields a '1+1: not found' error and empty output where dash gives '2'. HeredocBody#dollar dispatches only $( -> command_sub and $name -> param; it never checks for the second '(' the way Lexer::WordScanner#dollar_paren does. Surfaced (pre-existing) while making word segments polymorphic. Fix: mirror dollar_paren's $(( detection in HeredocBody, producing an ArithSegment. Verify differentially against dash.
close_reason: Implemented arithmetic expansion in here-document bodies by routing $((...)) to ArithSegment, with lexer unit coverage and a dash differential corpus case.

title: cd - should change to $OLDPWD (previous directory)
description: rush's cd does not implement the `cd -` special operand: POSIX/dash treat a single `-` as $OLDPWD (change to the previous working directory and print it). Currently rush treats `-` as a literal directory name and fails with 'No such file or directory'. Surfaced while moving the pwd invariant onto ShellState#move_to (which already maintains $OLDPWD). Fix: in Cd, when the operand is exactly '-', resolve it to state.environment.get('OLDPWD') (error if unset), cd there, and echo the new pwd. Verify differentially against dash.
close_reason: Implemented cd -: resolves to OLDPWD (falling back to logical current pwd before OLＤPWD exists), changes directory, prints destination, updates PWD/OLDPWD, and verifies against dash in the differential corpus.

title: rush >&n / <&n does not honour fds inherited from the parent process
description: Redirect duplication (n>&m, n<&m) resolves the source fd only against rush's own IoTable (0/1/2 plus fds opened in-shell via exec). An fd >= 3 inherited open from the parent is invisible, so 'true >&9' with fd 9 inherited-open errors (status 2) where dash dups the real fd and succeeds (0). POSIX/dash use the real OS fd table. Low priority: scripts rarely rely on inherited high fds, and the differential harness now closes them. Documenting the divergence.
